# Appendix: Supported Senses

<!-- Generated by 'WordSense.Builder generate-appendix' from corpus/senses and corpus/forms. Do not edit. -->

## How Answers Work

WordSense decides which **part of speech** a word carries in its sentence and, for a heteronym, which **pronunciation**.
The lemma is the dictionary form of the word (for example `record`); a word such as `records` is matched to its lemma
through the forms listed below. The answer for a word is a lemma, a part of speech and, for a heteronym only, a
pronunciation.

### Parts of Speech

The `PartOfSpeech` enumeration defines all eight classic parts of speech, but the shipped table only produces the four
listed here.

| Part of speech | Senses |
|----------------|--------|
| `Noun`         |    691 |
| `Verb`         |    725 |
| `Adjective`    |     93 |
| `Adverb`       |     12 |

### Pronunciation Meanings

A lemma is a **heteronym** when it has at least two distinct pronunciation meanings. Only then does an answer carry a
pronunciation: a short meaning id such as `guide` or `metal` for `lead`, and optionally a plain respelling. The library
has no phonetic data of its own; a consumer such as a speech synthesizer keeps its own pronunciations keyed by (lemma,
meaning). A lemma that is not a heteronym has no pronunciation in its answers.

### Forms

Inflected forms are mapped to their lemma by the forms map (`corpus/forms`), so `presents` is classified as a form of
`present`. A form may be restricted to some senses of the lemma, for example `led` can only be a form of the verb of
`lead`; such a restriction is shown in parentheses after the form. Forms that are not listed are unknown and are never
classified.

## Supported Lemmas

The library supports 744 lemmas with 1521 senses in total, listed alphabetically. Each lemma lists its parts of speech
and, for a heteronym, its pronunciation meanings and the inflected forms it recognizes. Under it, every sense gives its
part of speech, its meaning and respelling when it has them, and an example sentence in which the classified word is
shown in bold.
